questions.question: Which service model gives customers the greatest control over the operating system, middleware, and installed software?
questions.explanation: IaaS hands customers raw virtual infrastructure, so they control the OS and everything above it. PaaS and SaaS progressively abstract those layers away.

questions.question: Which service model lets developers deploy applications without managing servers, runtime environments, or the OS?
questions.explanation: PaaS manages the infrastructure and runtime, so developers only supply code and configuration. It trades some control for faster deployment.

questions.question: Which capability automatically adjusts cloud resources in real time to match demand, as opposed to planned growth capacity?
questions.explanation: Elasticity is automatic and reactive, adding or releasing resources as load changes. Scalability describes the system's overall capacity to grow.

questions.question: Which scaling approach adds more machines to share a workload instead of upgrading a single machine?
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling distributes load across more instances, usually behind a load balancer. It offers better fault tolerance than vertical scaling.

questions.question: Comparing containers and virtual machines, which starts faster and consumes fewer resources?
questions.explanation: Containers share the host kernel and skip booting a guest OS, so they start in seconds or less and pack more densely per host than VMs.

questions.question: In the IaaS shared responsibility model, which party is responsible for securing and patching the guest operating system?
questions.explanation: The provider secures the physical infrastructure and hypervisor, but the guest OS, applications, and data are the customer's responsibility in IaaS.

questions.question: Which strategy uses services from two or more public cloud providers at once rather than mixing public and private infrastructure?
questions.explanation: Multi-cloud distributes workloads across providers like AWS and Azure to avoid lock-in or use specialized services. Hybrid cloud instead mixes private and public resources.

questions.question: Which instance pricing model offers large discounts in exchange for one- or three-year commitments?
questions.explanation: Reserved instances and savings plans reward long-term commitments with discounts up to roughly 70 percent. They suit stable, predictable workloads.

questions.question: Which instance type provides spare compute capacity at steep discounts but can be interrupted on short notice?
questions.explanation: Spot instances sell unused capacity cheaply but may be reclaimed at any time. They fit interruptible work like batch processing and CI builds.

questions.question: Which cloud model bills per code invocation and execution duration rather than per running server?
questions.explanation: FaaS charges only while a function executes, down to millisecond granularity in some platforms. Idle time costs nothing, unlike VM-based billing.

questions.question: Increasing a single instance's CPU and RAM instead of adding instances is called what?
questions.explanation: Vertical scaling enlarges one machine's capacity. It is simple but hits hardware limits and usually requires downtime, unlike horizontal scaling.

questions.question: Which storage type stores unstructured data like images and backups as objects with metadata, rather than as raw disk volumes?
questions.explanation: Object storage (e.g., Amazon S3) stores data as objects in buckets with metadata and URLs. Block storage instead presents raw volumes to attach to instances.

questions.question: Which cloud component distributes incoming traffic across multiple instances to improve availability?
questions.explanation: Load balancers spread requests across healthy instances in one or more zones. They enable horizontal scaling and hide individual instance failures.

questions.question: Cloud computing converts large upfront hardware purchases into which category of spending?
questions.explanation: Cloud replaces CapEx (buying hardware) with OpEx (paying for services consumed). Costs scale with usage rather than requiring big initial investment.

questions.question: Which deployment model keeps sensitive workloads on-premises while bursting peak demand into a public cloud?
questions.explanation: Hybrid cloud links private and public environments so workloads can move between them. Cloud bursting handles traffic spikes while keeping data on-premises.
